en: The Apadāna of the Elder Mañjaripūjaka Chapter on the Praise-Worthy (Thomakavagga) 7 I was once a young man named Mañjarī, A youth endowed with great splendor. In the presence of the Buddha Vipassī, I offered a mañjarī-flower. Because of that root of merit performed by me, For eighty-four thousand aeons, I never fell into the states of misery; I experienced only happiness. Having passed through those aeons, I was reborn in the human world. There, too, I was always honored, Possessing great wealth and prosperity. Now, having been born in this final existence, I have attained the state of an Arhat. Through the offering of that single flower, I have reached the state of peace. I pay homage to the Blessed One, To the Teacher, the Fully Enlightened One. By the power of that wholesome deed, I have attained the fruit of Arhatship. Thus did the Elder Mañjaripūjaka speak his own ancient history.
Having fashioned a flower-cluster,
I set out upon the highway;
there I saw the foremost of recluses.
Honored by the community of monks,
with a clear heart and a joyful mind,
and with supreme rapture;
Taking them with both hands,
I offered them to the Buddha.
Ninety-two eons ago from now,
The flower that I offered in worship—
I do not know a state of misery;
this is the fruit of that flower-offering.
In this seventy-seventh aeon,
I was once a lord of the earth,
known by the name Jotiya.
A wheel-turning monarch of great power.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth].
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
It was in this way that the venerable elder Mañjaripūjaka recited these verses.
This is the seventh legend of the elder Mañjaripūjaka.
